## Exploration Roadmap

Welcome to **30 Days of Pharmaverse**. This project is a hands-on exploration of the modern clinical data science stack, designed for programmers and data scientists who want to dive deep into CDISC standards using the open-source Pharmaverse ecosystem.

Instead of a traditional course, think of this as a **guided tour** or a **developer's log**. Each day, we tackle a specific concept — from setting up a working environment to building complex ADaM datasets and producing TLF outputs — using industry-standard R packages like `admiral`, `xportr`, `metacore`, `rtables`, `tern`, and more.

```{r}
# Function to extract YAML frontmatter
extract_yaml <- function(file_path) {
  lines <- readLines(file_path)
  yaml_delims <- which(lines == "---")

  if (length(yaml_delims) >= 2) {
    yaml_content <- lines[(yaml_delims[1] + 1):(yaml_delims[2] - 1)]
    yaml_str <- paste(yaml_content, collapse = "\n")
    tryCatch({
      yaml::yaml.load(yaml_str)
    }, error = function(e) {
      list(title = "Unknown", subtitle = "Unknown")
    })
  } else {
    list(title = "Unknown", subtitle = "Unknown")
  }
}

# Function to generate table for a week
generate_week_table <- function(week_dir, week_num, week_title) {
  day_files <- list.files(week_dir, pattern = "^day\\d+\\.qmd$", full.names = TRUE) %>%
    sort()

  if (length(day_files) == 0) return(invisible(NULL))

  course_data <- day_files %>%
    lapply(function(file) {
      yaml_meta <- extract_yaml(file)
      day_num <- str_extract(basename(file), "\\d+")
      list(
        day_num = as.numeric(day_num),
        file = file,
        title = yaml_meta$title,
        subtitle = yaml_meta$subtitle,
        packages = packages_map[[day_num]] %||% ""
      )
    }) %>%
    bind_rows() %>%
    arrange(day_num) %>%
    mutate(
      html_file = paste0(week_dir, "/day", day_num, ".html"),
      day_link = paste0("**[Day ", day_num, "](", html_file, ")**"),
      topic = str_remove(title, "^Day \\d+: "),
      focus_area = subtitle
    )

  cat(paste0("### Week ", week_num, ": ", week_title, "\n\n"))
  cat("| Day | Topic | Deep Dive | Key Packages |\n")
  cat("|---|---|---|---|\n")

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(course_data))) {
    row <- course_data[i, ]
    cat(sprintf("| %s | %s | %s | %s |\n",
                row$day_link,
                row$topic,
                row$focus_area,
                row$packages))
  }
  cat("\n")
}

# Generate tables for all four weeks
generate_week_table("week1", 1, "SDTM Fundamentals & Core R Skills")
generate_week_table("week2", 2, "Production SDTM & Validation")
generate_week_table("week3", 3, "ADaM Deep Dive & Admiral Mastery")
generate_week_table("week4", 4, "ADaM Advanced & TLF Production")
```

## What You'll Explore

This journey covers the essential toolkit for modern clinical programming in R:

- **SDTM & ADaM Standards**: Understanding the structure and intent of CDISC-standardised data.
- **Pharmaverse Tools**: Hands-on work with `admiral`, `pharmaversesdtm`, `pharmaverseadam`, `xportr`, `sdtm.oak`, `sdtmchecks`, `metacore`, and more.
- **ADaM Construction**: Building ADSL, ADAE, ADLB, ADVS, ADTTE, ADCM, ADEX, and ADRS from SDTM using `admiral` and `admiralonco`.
- **TLF Production**: Tables, listings, and figures using `rtables`/`tern`, `r2rtf`, `flextable`+`officer`, `gtsummary`, `tfrmt`, `rlistings`, and `ggsurvfit`.
- **ARD-First Workflows**: Using `cards` and `cardx` to produce tidy Analysis Results Datasets that separate computation from formatting.
- **QC & Traceability**: Unit testing with `testthat`, cell-level traceability with `Tplyr`, audit logging with `logrx`, and metadata-driven export with `xportr`.

## The Toolkit

**Prerequisites:**
- Comfort with R and the `tidyverse`
- A curiosity about clinical trials and data standards

**Core Packages:**
```r
# SDTM layer
install.packages(c("admiral", "pharmaversesdtm", "pharmaverseadam",
                   "sdtm.oak", "sdtmchecks", "datacutr",
                   "metacore", "metatools", "xportr", "haven"))

# ADaM extensions
install.packages("admiralonco")

# TLF — tables
install.packages(c("rtables", "tern", "r2rtf", "flextable", "officer",
                   "gtsummary", "tfrmt", "Tplyr", "rlistings"))

# TLF — figures
install.packages(c("ggplot2", "ggsurvfit", "patchwork"))

# ARD & QC
install.packages(c("cards", "cardx", "testthat", "logrx"))
```

## **⚠️ Important Disclaimer**

This project is a **personal initiative** created for **learning and exploratory purposes only**. It is in no way affiliated with, endorsed by, sponsored by, funded by, or assisted by any organisation or company at any capacity.

* This project draws heavily from open-source projects, Pharmaverse examples, public repositories, and official CDISC documentation.
* Significant portions of the code and content have been created with assistance from **Large Language Models (LLMs)** and refined through human review and intervention.
* Examples and patterns are adapted from established best practices in the R and clinical programming communities.

**Learners are strongly encouraged to:**

1. **Think critically** — Don't just copy-paste code. Understand *why* each step exists.
2. **Verify independently** — Check code against official Pharmaverse documentation and CDISC standards.
3. **Test thoroughly** — Validate any code in your own environment before use in any context.
4. **Consult experts** — When implementing for real clinical trials, seek guidance from qualified statisticians and data managers.

The views, opinions, code, and materials shared in this project are solely for exploratory and learning purposes and do not guarantee accuracy, correctness, or compliance with any standard. They do not represent the positions of any external organisation and should not be treated as guidance for any formal or regulated use without independent verification.

## Community & Resources

- [Pharmaverse.org](https://pharmaverse.org) — The central hub for open-source clinical R packages.
- [CDISC.org](https://www.cdisc.org) — The official standards body for clinical data.
- [Admiral Documentation](https://pharmaverse.github.io/admiral/) — The flagship ADaM derivation package.
- [r4csr.org](https://r4csr.org) — Open-access book: *R for Clinical Study Reports* (Zhang et al.).
- [pharmaverse TLG Catalogue](https://pharmaverse.github.io/TLG-Catalog) — Reference TLF outputs from the pharmaverse stack.
- [R Consortium R Submission Working Group](https://rconsortium.github.io/submissions-wg/) — Ongoing work on R-based submissions (pilot projects, not formal FDA guidance).
